settings.title: Warning Signs: Is It Time To Replace Your Electrical Panel?

settings.editor:
Listed below are some key warning signs that your electrical panel might be reaching its limit and in need of replacement. Ignoring warning signs can lead to safety hazards, inconvenience, and even potential damage to your home's electrical system.

  • Frequent circuit breaker tripping signifies an overload, often indicating your panel can't handle the current electrical demands. This can damage appliances and pose fire hazards.
  • Flickering or Dimming Lights can be unsettling and disrupt your daily routine. While a loose bulb might be the culprit sometimes, it can also point to a larger issue like an overloaded or malfunctioning electrical panel.
  • Electrical panels typically have a lifespan of around 20-25 years. If your property is older, chances are your panel is nearing the end of its useful life and might require replacement to ensure continued safety and efficiency.
  • Buildings built before the mid-1960s might have aluminum wiring. This type of wiring is susceptible to overheating and poses potential fire hazards. Upgrading to a panel compatible with copper wiring is crucial to address this safety concern.
  • Upgrading with new appliances, fixtures, or a pool increases your electrical load. If your panel is already strained, these additions can push it beyond its capacity, necessitating an upgrade to handle the additional demands safely.

Please don't wait for electrical issues to disrupt your life and compromise your safety. Contact us right away for a free consultation and expert advice.

settings.title: Keeping Your New Panel Thriving: Maintenance Tips For Long-Lasting Performance

settings.editor:
Congratulations on your new electrical panel! It's an investment in your home's safety and efficiency. Here are some simple yet effective maintenance tips To help it function optimally for years to come:  

  • Twice a year, visually inspect your panel for any signs of damage, such as rust, corrosion, cracks, or burning odors. If you notice anything unusual, contact a qualified electrician immediately.
  • Ensure there's at least 3 feet of clearance around the entire panel. This allows for proper ventilation and prevents objects from blocking access or creating a fire hazard.
  • Clearly label each breaker with the corresponding circuit it controls. This makes troubleshooting and future maintenance easier and safer.
  • Don't plug in too many appliances or electronics into a single circuit. This can overload the circuit and trip the breaker, or worse, lead to overheating and potential fire dangers.
  • Resist the urge to attempt any electrical work yourself. Contact our licensed electricians for any electrical concerns or repairs. We offer 24/7 service for your protection and peace of mind.
